summary: Checked whether any FOR_SALE/SCHEDULED, non-expired, non-dormant, non-draft menu item has 2+ line builds at the same HDR after excluding is_multiple_usage=true and is_multiple_version=true line builds. Result: zero cases (verified against 845 qualifying items / 1233 versions, 9968 item-version x restaurant pairs checked, cross-checked with and without preset exclusion). Found and corrected a methodology trap: grouping by item_number+restaurant without item_version_id falsely flagged ~100+ false-positive duplicates that were actually just current-vs-upcoming-scheduled-version line build changes, not real concurrent conflicts. Only 3 same-version same-HDR non-flagged duplicates exist system-wide, all on long-DORMANT/NOT_SOLD items from 2022-2023. Directly supports the same-day Line Build Multi-Version & Multi-Usage Toggles deprecation analysis: confirms no third undocumented mechanism produces duplicate line builds outside the two known toggles.
learned: Grouping duplicate-line-build checks by item_number+restaurant alone is wrong; must include item_version_id, since an item can have both a current FINAL and a future SCHEDULED qualifying version simultaneously, each carrying its own distinct line build for the same restaurant (sequential, not conflicting).
sold_status has 4 real values: FOR_SALE, SCHEDULED, NOT_SOLD, N/A - confirmed against Z01-Resource/CB-business/core/item-lifecycle.md §7.1.
item_line_build / item_line_builds has no non-sensitive fallback - secure-recipe-prod access is genuinely required.

summary: Bonnie corrected a modeling error: item_line_builds.restaurant_id is NOT the physical HDR - one HDR hosts many restaurant (brand-instance) records, mapped via wonder-dw-prod-brd.forecast.active_service_calendar_v2 / dim_hdrs (hdr_id / hdr_name / hdr_code), not 1:1. Re-ran the same-HDR duplicate-line-build check by resolving restaurant_id to hdr_id (exact join for 96 percent of rows, fuzzy hdr_name/hdr_code text match against dim_hdrs for the remaining new/unpublished-restaurant rows). Revised result: found 6 real cases (not zero) where a qualifying menu item has 2 different line builds at the same physical HDR (Upper East Side) after excluding is_multiple_usage/is_multiple_version=true builds - items 8008516, 8010431, 8010435, 8010437, 8010438, 8010439. Root cause: a single UNPUBLISHED ghost restaurant record literally named DO NOT USE Alanza Upper East Side (restaurant_id bb44c9c5-a7f3-4338-94e7-2f14192c2998) still carries live LINE_BUILD_CREATED line builds for 10 current/upcoming menu items, 6 of which now diverge from the line build used by the restaurant that actually replaced it at that HDR. Also found 4 other unpublished/temp restaurant records with orphaned-but-harmless (identical-content) line builds at other HDRs, worth cleanup but not causing a live conflict.
learned: item_line_builds.restaurant_id is brand-instance-at-a-location, not the physical HDR; must resolve via active_service_calendar_v2 (exact, about 96 percent coverage) plus fuzzy hdr_name/hdr_code matching against dim_hdrs for new/pre-launch or unpublished restaurants (about 4 percent) to get true HDR-level grouping.

wonder-dw-prod-brd.dw.dim_hdr_restaurants looked like a clean restaurant-to-hdr bridge but is NOT reliable - restaurant_id there is many-to-many with hdr_id for most rows (looks like brand-level or a messy historical dump), contradicts the vetted schema doc's 1:1 claim; do not use it for this kind of mapping without further validation.

Orphaned line builds on UNPUBLISHED ghost restaurant records (e.g. explicitly named DO NOT USE) are a real, findable data-hygiene pattern in Cookbook line build data and can surface as false same-HDR conflicts.
followups: Consider proposing cleanup/deletion of line builds tied to bb44c9c5-a7f3-4338-94e7-2f14192c2998 and the 4 other unpublished ghost restaurant records identified.
Consider a recurring health check: qualifying menu items x unpublished restaurant records still carrying LINE_BUILD_CREATED configs.
